drivingQuestion: Is 'slaughter applies to its kind' really the criterion for whether slaughter purifies from carcass impurity, given that the baraita says an eight-month-old fetus born alive has slaughter in its kind and is still not purified?
outcomeNote: The unit ends with the difficulty from the baraita standing; no answer is contained in this packet.

segments.he: בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי. וְהָתַנְיָא: בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי יוֹכִיחַ, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּמִינוֹ שְׁחִיטָה – אֵין שְׁחִיטָתוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ.
segments.en: § The mishna states that «an eight-»month«-old» fetus that was born «alive» is not rendered ritually pure by slaughtering it. The reason given is that the concept of permitting an animal through slaughter is never stated with regard to that kind of animal. The Gemara challenges: But «isn’t it taught» in a baraita in a discussion about whether slaughter renders a tereifa pure from the impurity of a carcass: «An eight-»month«-old» fetus that was born «alive will prove» the point, «as even though there are» other animals «of that kind» that are permitted through «slaughter, its slaughter does not render it pure» from having the impurity of a carcass. This refutes the claim that the issue of slaughter rendering an animal pure from having the impurity of a carcass is a function of whether or not the concept of slaughter applies to that kind of animal.
